```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(knitr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(kableExtra)
  library(openxlsx)
})

rda_path <- here::here("projects/dhis_hospital_mortality/dhis_results.rda")
if (!file.exists(rda_path)) stop("Run projects/dhis_hospital_mortality/wrangling.R first.")
load(rda_path)

fmt <- function(x, d = 0) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","))
}

# Excel-style cohort grid: rows = year of insertion, columns = calendar year.
# Each cell = units inserted x weight for that many years since insertion.
# Adding down a column gives the adjusted CYP for that calendar year.
grid_table <- function(units, ins_years, w, cal_years, std, caption,
                       scale = 1, d = 0) {
  k <- outer(ins_years, cal_years, function(s, t) t - s)
  ok <- k >= 0 & k < length(w)
  wk <- matrix(0, length(ins_years), length(cal_years))
  wk[ok] <- w[k[ok] + 1]
  m <- units * wk * scale
  lifetime <- units * sum(w) * scale
  after <- pmax(lifetime - rowSums(m), 0)
  after[after < 1e-6] <- 0
  show_after <- any(after > 1e-6)

  adj <- colSums(m)
  std_rows <- lapply(std, function(f) {
    v <- numeric(length(cal_years))
    hit <- cal_years %in% ins_years
    v[hit] <- f * units[match(cal_years[hit], ins_years)] * scale
    v
  })
  diff_row <- adj - std_rows[[1]]

  body <- ifelse(m == 0, "", fmt(m, d))
  mk <- function(v, tot) c(fmt(v, d), fmt(tot, d), if (show_after) "")
  out <- cbind(body, Within = fmt(rowSums(m), d))
  if (show_after) out <- cbind(out, After = fmt(after, d))
  out <- rbind(
    out,
    mk(adj, sum(adj)),
    do.call(rbind, lapply(std_rows, function(v) mk(v, sum(v)))),
    mk(diff_row, sum(diff_row))
  )
  row_lab <- c(
    paste0("Inserted ", ins_years, " (", fmt(units), " units)"),
    "ADJUSTED CYP in the year (add down the column)",
    names(std),
    "Difference: adjusted minus first standard row"
  )
  hdr <- c("", cal_years, if (show_after) c("Total in table", "Falls after table") else "Total")
  nr <- length(ins_years)

  kbl(cbind(row_lab, out), col.names = hdr, align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(out))),
      caption = caption, row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12, position = "left") |>
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#d9d9d9") |>
    column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) |>
    row_spec(nr + 1, bold = TRUE, background = "#e2efda") |>
    row_spec(nr + 2:(length(std) + 1), background = "#fff2cc") |>
    row_spec(nr + length(std) + 2, italic = TRUE)
}

excel_table <- function(df, caption, align = NULL, font_size = 12, bold_last = FALSE) {
  tb <- kbl(df, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
            align = align) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, font_size = font_size, position = "left") |>
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#d9d9d9")
  if (bold_last) tb <- tb |> row_spec(nrow(df), bold = TRUE, background = "#e2efda")
  tb
}
```

## Summary

**Question.** Does allocating long-acting-method CYP to the years protected,
rather than the insertion year, change annual programme CYP or its correlation
with births?

**Comparison.** The baseline credits all CYP in the distribution year. Rob's
request changes the pill and implant factors and redistributes implant and IUCD
protection over later years using decaying weights. Programme comparisons
exclude condoms; condom CYP is shown separately.

**Main findings.** The request specifies redistribution and revised factors.
The displayed implementation also uses an analyst-selected pre-2015 warm-up,
so differences from baseline reflect all three. Correlations with next-year
births are descriptive; ten annual observations cannot establish a causal
relationship or validate the assumed decay weights.

**Contents.**

| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | Standard baseline and factors in Rob's request |
| 2 | Weights |
| 3 | Use case A: implants |
| 4 | Use cases B (IUCD) and C (short-acting methods, sterilisation) |
| 5 | National implant data |
| 6 | Standard baseline versus Rob's request, excluding condoms |
| 7 | Compare both CYP series with births |
| 8 | Limits and decisions |

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading the grids
Each row is a group of insertions (a cohort) and each column is a calendar year.
A cell is the protection that cohort gives in that year. Add down a column for
that year's CYP. Add across a row for the cohort's total.
:::

## Step 1. Standard CYP

Standard CYP is units multiplied by a fixed factor, credited to the year of
distribution.

```{r}
#| label: step1
step1 <- data.frame(
  Method = c("Oral pill", "Sub-dermal implant", "Copper IUCD"),
  `What is counted` = c("Pill cycles", "Insertions", "Insertions"),
  `Units in 2021` = c("1,200", "100", "100"),
  `Standard factor` = c("1/15", "3.5", "4.6"),
  `Rob-request factor` = c("1/12", "2.5", "4.6"),
  `Standard CYP in 2021` = c("80", "350", "460"),
  `Rob-request CYP in 2021` = c("100", "250", "460"),
  `Years of protection` = c("About 1", "3", "10"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
excel_table(step1, "Standard baseline and factors specified in Rob's request.",
            align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
```

The request specifies 12 pill cycles per CYP and 2.5 CYP per implant; the
baseline uses 15 cycles and 3.5 CYP per implant. Confirm the pill product before
applying 12 cycles: the methods note distinguishes combined-pill cycles from
progestin-only packs.

The adjusted scenario moves implant and IUCD protection to the years it is
expected to occur. The following grids make those contributions checkable.

## Step 2. Weights

Adjusted CYP uses a weight per year since insertion: year 0 is the year of
insertion, year 1 the next year, and so on.

```{r}
#| label: step2
fullm <- ADJUSTED_CYP_MATRIX[short_label %in% c("Sub-dermal implant", "IUCD")]
wide <- dcast(fullm, short_label ~ protection_year, value.var = "adjusted_cyp")
yrs <- setdiff(names(wide), "short_label")
wide[, Total := rowSums(.SD, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = yrs]
wtab <- wide[, lapply(.SD, function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2))),
             by = short_label]
setnames(wtab, c("short_label", yrs, "Total"),
         c("Method", paste("Year", yrs), "Total CYP per insertion"))
excel_table(as.data.frame(wtab),
            "Rob-request allocation weights per insertion for long-acting methods.",
            align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(wtab) - 1)), font_size = 11)
```

Rules:

1. The weights add up to the method's CYP factor, so a cohort's lifetime CYP is
   unchanged.
2. The weights fall over time, because some women stop using the method.
3. Implants and IUCDs are the only methods spread. Injectables, pills and
   condoms last about a year or less and are credited in the distribution year.
   Sterilisation is permanent but is also credited in the procedure year (see
   Step 4).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Weights are assumptions
Rob supplied the implant weights (1.00, 0.80, 0.70) and the first two IUCD
weights (0.85, 0.75). The rest of the IUCD profile is an assumed steady fall
that totals 4.6. Replace them with local continuation data when available.
:::

## Step 3. Use case A: implants

Suppose 100, 120, 90 and 110 implants are inserted in 2021 to 2024, and none
before or after. Each insertion gives 1.00 CYP in its own year, 0.80 the next
year and 0.70 the year after.

```{r}
#| label: usecase-implant
grid_table(
  units = c(100, 120, 90, 110), ins_years = 2021:2024,
  w = c(1.00, 0.80, 0.70), cal_years = 2021:2026,
  std = c("Standard baseline (3.5 CYP, credited in insertion year)" = 3.5),
  caption = "Use case A: implant CYP by calendar year, standard baseline versus Rob's requested allocation."
)
```

**2023 column:**
90 × 1.00 (2023 insertions) + 120 × 0.80 (2022 insertions, second year) +
100 × 0.70 (2021 insertions, third year) = 90 + 96 + 70 = **256 CYP**.

The baseline puts 315 CYP in 2023 and nothing after 2024. Rob's requested
allocation puts 256 in 2023, 151 in 2025 and 77 in 2026. Across these cohorts,
the baseline totals 1,470 CYP (3.5 per insertion); the request totals 1,050
(2.5 per insertion). The difference therefore includes both the factor change
and redistribution.

## Step 4. More use cases

### Use case B: copper IUCD

Suppose 100 IUCDs are inserted in each of 2021, 2022 and 2023. The weights run
for ten years, so protection builds up and continues well after the last
insertion.

```{r}
#| label: usecase-iucd
iucd_w <- ADJUSTED_CYP_MATRIX[short_label == "IUCD"][order(protection_year)]$adjusted_cyp
grid_table(
  units = c(100, 100, 100), ins_years = 2021:2023,
  w = iucd_w, cal_years = 2021:2032,
  std = c("Standard CYP (all credited in insertion year)" = 4.6),
  caption = "Use case B: IUCD CYP by calendar year, standard versus adjusted.",
  d = 0
) |> scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

In 2023, standard CYP is 460 (the 2023 insertions only). Adjusted CYP is
100 × 0.85 + 100 × 0.75 + 100 × 0.65 = **225**: the 2023 cohort is in its first
year and the 2021 and 2022 cohorts are in their third and second. The
remaining 910 of the 1,380 CYP falls in 2024–2032.
### Use case C: injectables, pills, condoms and sterilisation

```{r}
#| label: usecase-short
short_tab <- data.frame(
  Method = c("Medroxyprogesterone (DMPA)", "Norethisterone (NET-EN)", "Oral pill",
             "Male / female condom", "Sterilisation (F or M)"),
  Unit = c("Injection", "Injection", "Cycle", "Condom", "Procedure"),
  `Units in 2021` = c("1,200", "1,200", "1,200", "12,000", "10"),
  `Standard baseline CYP (2021)` = c("300", "200", "80", "100", "100"),
  `Rob-request CYP (2021)` = c("300", "200", "100", "100", "100"),
  `Rob-request CYP (2022 onwards)` = c("0", "0", "0", "0", "0"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
excel_table(short_tab,
            "Use case C: short-duration methods are not redistributed; the pill factor differs by scenario.",
            align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 4)))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sterilisation
Sterilisation is permanent and is credited 10 CYP in the procedure year, not
spread. This is inconsistent with spreading implants and IUCDs and affects
comparisons with births. Decide whether to spread it or report it separately.
:::

## Step 5. The real data: implants, 2015–2025

The same layout with national DHIS counts of sub-dermal implants inserted.
Rows are insertion years, columns are calendar years, and figures are thousands
of CYP. The requested allocation uses the pipeline's pre-2015 warm-up.

```{r}
#| label: real-data-prep
# All inputs come from wrangling.R, which already applies the one documented
# data correction (see below).
imp_w <- ADJUSTED_CYP_MATRIX[short_label == "Sub-dermal implant"][order(protection_year)]$adjusted_cyp
imp <- adjusted_cyp_lag_buildup[
  scenario == "Proposed new: steady-state initialization" &
    short_label == "Sub-dermal implant",
  .(year = source_year, n = services)
][, unique(.SD, by = "year")][order(year)]

# Hand calculation of the weighted sum must match the pipeline output.
n_by_year <- setNames(imp$n, imp$year)
check_years <- 2015:2025
hand <- vapply(check_years, function(t) {
  v <- n_by_year[as.character(t - seq_along(imp_w) + 1)]
  sum(imp_w * ifelse(is.na(v), 0, v))
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  unname(hand),
  agg_adjusted_cyp_method_annual[
    scenario == "Proposed new: steady-state initialization" &
      short_label == "Sub-dermal implant" & year %in% check_years][order(year)]$adjusted_cyp
)))

fix <- data_corrections_log[1]
```

```{r}
#| label: real-implant-grid
grid_table(
  units = imp$n, ins_years = imp$year, w = imp_w, cal_years = 2015:2025,
    std = c("Rob-request factor, credited in insertion year (2.5)" = 2.5,
      "A. Standard baseline (3.5)" = 3.5),
  scale = 1e-3,
    caption = "National sub-dermal implants: baseline and requested factor versus decay-weighted CYP, thousands (2025 corrected)."
) |> scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

For each calendar year, multiply that year's insertions by 1.00, the prior
year's by 0.80, and the insertions two years earlier by 0.70; add the
contributions. Pre-2015 rows use the 2015 count as the assumed warm-up. The
adjusted annual totals are checked against the pipeline; the baseline column
credits 3.5 CYP per insertion in its insertion year.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Corrected reporting error
`r fix$facility` reports `r fmt(fix$reported_value)` implants for
`r format(fix$period_date, "%B %Y")`, against a typical `r fmt(fix$replacement_value)`
per month. That entry is `r round(100 * fix$reported_value / fix$national_annual_before)`%
of the reported 2025 national total. `wrangling.R` replaces it with the
facility's typical monthly value, so every page uses the corrected data. The
correction is recorded in `data_corrections_log`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: real-correction-table
corr_tab <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Reported national implants, 2025", "Corrected national implants, 2025",
           "Removed"),
  Value = fmt(c(fix$national_annual_before, fix$national_annual_after, fix$excess_removed))
)
excel_table(corr_tab, "Effect of the correction on 2025 implant insertions.",
            align = c("l", "r"))
```

Pre-2015 insertion counts are not observed. The requested series initializes
those cohorts by carrying the 2015 count backward; this assumption affects the
early adjusted totals (see Step 8).

## Step 6. Standard baseline versus the request implementation

Both series use the same corrected national DHIS data and exclude condoms. Rob's
request specifies revised factors and decay-weighted allocation. Since DHIS
starts in 2015, the displayed implementation additionally uses a steady-state
pre-2015 initialization; that is an analysis assumption, not part of the
verbatim request. The annual difference combines factor changes, redistribution
and initialization.

```{r}
#| label: all-methods
pc <- copy(programme_cyp_comparison)[order(year)]
disp <- pc[, .(
  Year = year,
  `A. Standard baseline` = fmt(standard_cyp / 1e3),
  `B. Request implementation` = fmt(full_proposal_cyp / 1e3),
  `Difference (B - A)` = fmt((full_proposal_cyp - standard_cyp) / 1e3),
  `Difference from baseline (%)` = fmt(full_vs_standard_pct, 1)
)]
excel_table(as.data.frame(disp),
            "Annual programme CYP excluding condoms, thousands (2025 corrected).",
            align = c("l", rep("r", 4)), font_size = 11) |> scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

Rob's request specifies 12 pill cycles per CYP, 2.5 CYP per implant, and
decay-weighted allocation for implants and IUCDs. The pre-2015 initialization
assumes 2015 counts in earlier years; it is not observed historical data.

### Intervention contributions by year

Each row is one intervention in one year. CYP and CYP per 1,000 women aged
15–49 are shown for the standard baseline, equal spreading, decay with standard
factors, and the full request implementation. Condoms are excluded. Methods
that are not spread remain unchanged apart from any revised factor in the full
request.

Equal spreading divides each standard lifetime factor evenly across its
protection years. The spread, decay, and request columns use the 2015 count to
initialize pre-2015 cohorts where needed; this is an explicit assumption, not
observed historical data. Existing standard CYP values are not modified.

```{r}
#| label: intervention-cyp-table

table_years <- 2015:2025
condom_labels <- c("Female condom", "Male condom")
standard_method <- as.data.table(copy(agg_cyp_national_annual))[
  !short_label %chin% condom_labels & year %in% table_years,
  .(intervention = short_label, year, standard_cyp = cyp)
]

method_factors <- as.data.table(copy(REDISTRIBUTION_ONLY_CYP_MATRIX))[
  , .(standard_factor = sum(adjusted_cyp), max_lag = max(protection_year)),
  by = short_label
]
method_names <- method_factors$short_label
source_units <- merge(
  standard_method,
  method_factors[, .(intervention = short_label, standard_factor)],
  by = "intervention"
)[, .(intervention, source_year = year, units = standard_cyp / standard_factor)]

backfill_keys <- method_factors[max_lag > 0,
  .(source_year = seq.int(min(table_years) - max_lag, min(table_years) - 1L)),
  by = .(intervention = short_label, max_lag)
][, .(intervention, source_year)]
backfill_units <- merge(
  backfill_keys,
  source_units[source_year == min(table_years), .(intervention, units)],
  by = "intervention"
)
source_units <- rbindlist(list(source_units, backfill_units), use.names = TRUE)

allocate_for_table <- function(weight_matrix, value_name) {
  weight_matrix <- as.data.table(copy(weight_matrix))[
    short_label %chin% method_names,
    .(intervention = short_label, protection_year, weight = adjusted_cyp)
  ]
  merge(source_units, weight_matrix, by = "intervention", allow.cartesian = TRUE)[
    , year := source_year + protection_year
  ][year %in% table_years,
    .(value = sum(units * weight, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = .(intervention, year)
  ] |> setnames("value", value_name)
}

even_spread_matrix <- as.data.table(copy(REDISTRIBUTION_ONLY_CYP_MATRIX))[
  , adjusted_cyp := sum(adjusted_cyp) / .N, by = short_label
]
even_spread_method <- allocate_for_table(even_spread_matrix, "even_spread_cyp")
decay_method <- allocate_for_table(REDISTRIBUTION_ONLY_CYP_MATRIX, "decay_cyp")
request_method <- allocate_for_table(ADJUSTED_CYP_MATRIX, "request_cyp")

intervention_cyp <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(
  x, y, by = c("intervention", "year"), all = TRUE
), list(standard_method, even_spread_method, decay_method, request_method))
intervention_cyp <- merge(
  intervention_cyp,
  as.data.table(copy(agg_wra_population_annual))[year %in% table_years],
  by = "year"
)
cyp_columns <- c("standard_cyp", "even_spread_cyp", "decay_cyp", "request_cyp")
setnafill(intervention_cyp, cols = cyp_columns, fill = 0)
intervention_cyp[, `:=`(
  standard_rate = standard_cyp / wra_population * 1000,
  even_spread_rate = even_spread_cyp / wra_population * 1000,
  decay_rate = decay_cyp / wra_population * 1000,
  request_rate = request_cyp / wra_population * 1000
)]

intervention_totals <- intervention_cyp[, lapply(.SD, sum, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = year, .SDcols = c(cyp_columns, "standard_rate", "even_spread_rate", "decay_rate", "request_rate")]
intervention_totals[, intervention := "Total (excluding condoms)"]
intervention_cyp <- rbindlist(list(intervention_cyp, intervention_totals), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)
setorder(intervention_cyp, year, intervention)

scenario_keys <- c(
  "A. Standard", "E. Even spread (no decay)", "C. Timing only", "D. Full proposal"
)
scenario_columns <- c("standard_cyp", "even_spread_cyp", "decay_cyp", "request_cyp")
for (i in seq_along(scenario_keys)) {
  saved_total <- cyp_decay_series[
    group == "All methods" & measure == scenario_keys[i],
    .(year, cyp_value)
  ][order(year)]$cyp_value
  table_total <- intervention_totals[order(year), get(scenario_columns[i])]
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(table_total), unname(saved_total))))
}

cyp_download <- intervention_cyp[, .(
  Year = year,
  Intervention = intervention,
  `Standard CYP` = standard_cyp,
  `Standard rate per 1,000 women 15-49` = standard_rate,
  `Even spread CYP` = even_spread_cyp,
  `Even spread rate per 1,000 women 15-49` = even_spread_rate,
  `Decay CYP, standard factors` = decay_cyp,
  `Decay rate per 1,000 women 15-49` = decay_rate,
  `Full request CYP` = request_cyp,
  `Full request rate per 1,000 women 15-49` = request_rate
)]

scenario_notes <- data.frame(
  Scenario = c("Standard", "Even spread", "Decay, standard factors", "Full request", "Rates and scope"),
  Definition = c(
    "Existing standard CYP; all CYP credited in the service year.",
    "Standard lifetime factors allocated evenly across the protection years.",
    "Standard factors retained; implant and IUCD CYP allocated with decay weights.",
    "Decay allocation with the requested pill and implant factors.",
    "CYP per 1,000 women aged 15-49; condoms excluded."
  ),
  Assumptions = c(
    "No pre-2015 carryover.",
    "2015 counts initialize pre-2015 cohorts where needed.",
    "2015 counts initialize pre-2015 cohorts where needed.",
    "2015 counts initialize pre-2015 cohorts where needed.",
    "Source counts and existing standard CYP values are unchanged."
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

workbook_path <- here::here("projects/dhis_hospital_mortality/dhis_cyp_by_intervention_year.xlsx")
workbook <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(workbook, "CYP by intervention")
writeDataTable(workbook, "CYP by intervention", cyp_download,
               tableName = "InterventionCYP", tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
freezePane(workbook, "CYP by intervention", firstRow = TRUE, firstCol = TRUE)
setColWidths(workbook, "CYP by intervention", cols = seq_len(ncol(cyp_download)), widths = "auto")
addWorksheet(workbook, "Scenario notes")
writeDataTable(workbook, "Scenario notes", scenario_notes,
               tableName = "ScenarioNotes", tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2")
setColWidths(workbook, "Scenario notes", cols = 1:3, widths = c(26, 68, 68))
saveWorkbook(workbook, workbook_path, overwrite = TRUE)

display_table <- copy(cyp_download)
numeric_columns <- names(display_table)[vapply(display_table, is.numeric, logical(1))]
display_table[, (numeric_columns) := lapply(.SD, function(x) formatC(
  x, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","
)), .SDcols = numeric_columns]
```

[Download the intervention-by-year CYP workbook](dhis_cyp_by_intervention_year.xlsx). The workbook includes a filterable data sheet and scenario notes.

```{r}
#| label: intervention-cyp-display
excel_table(
  as.data.frame(display_table),
  "Annual CYP and CYP rates by intervention and scenario; condoms excluded.",
  align = c("r", "l", rep("r", 8)), font_size = 10
) |> scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "600px")
```

```{r}
#| label: condom-share
ctab <- copy(cyp_condom_share_annual)
excel_table(
  data.frame(
    Year = ctab$year,
    `Non-condom standard CYP (thousands)` = fmt(ctab$noncondom_cyp / 1e3),
    `Condom CYP at 100% use (thousands)` = fmt(ctab$condom_cyp / 1e3),
    `Condoms as % of all CYP` = fmt(ctab$condom_share_pct, 1),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  "Why condoms are excluded from the headline comparison (2025 implant correction applied).",
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

Condoms account for 45–72% of all CYP if every distributed condom is counted as
used. They are not redistributed, and reporting shifts from facility to district
level in 2018. They are excluded from the baseline/request comparison and shown
separately here.

## Step 7. Compare both CYP series with births

This descriptive comparison uses only the **standard baseline** and the
**request implementation**. The latter combines Rob's revised factors and
decay-weighted allocation with the analysis's assumed pre-2015 carryover; the
correlation difference cannot identify the contribution of any one component.
Births are facility births in N+1, shown as counts and crude rates per 1,000
women aged 15–49. Condoms are excluded from the programme total.

```{r}
#| label: decay-helpers
al_next <- "Births in following year (N+1)"
al_prev <- "Births in previous year (N-1)"
mcol <- c("A. Standard" = "#6a3d9a", "D. Full proposal" = "#1b9e77")
rv <- function(g, m, bs = "Counts", vw = "Yearly values", al = al_next) {
  sprintf("%.2f", cyp_decay_correlation[group == g & measure == m & basis == bs &
                                          view == vw & alignment == al, correlation])
}
jk_request <- function(g, bs = "Counts") {
  round(10 * cyp_decay_correlation[
    group == g & measure == "D. Full proposal" & basis == bs &
      view == "Yearly values" & alignment == al_next,
    jackknife_stronger
  ])
}

cor_block <- function(vw, al, bs) {
  d <- cyp_decay_correlation[view == vw & alignment == al & basis == bs &
                               measure %in% names(mcol)]
  w <- dcast(d, group ~ measure, value.var = "correlation")
  ci <- d[measure == "D. Full proposal", .(group, ci = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", ci_low, ci_high))]
  w <- merge(w, ci, by = "group")
  jkv <- d[measure == "D. Full proposal", .(group, jk = jackknife_stronger)]
  w <- merge(w, jkv, by = "group")
  w <- w[order(group)]
  out <- data.frame(
    Group = as.character(w$group),
    `A. Standard baseline` = sprintf("%.2f", w$`A. Standard`),
    `B. Request implementation` = sprintf("%.2f", w$`D. Full proposal`),
    `B minus A` = sprintf("%+.2f", w$`D. Full proposal` - w$`A. Standard`),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  if (vw == "Yearly values") {
    out[["Leave-one-year-out: request stronger than baseline (of 10)"]] <- ifelse(
      is.na(w$jk), "", round(10 * w$jk))
  }
  out
}
```

Values closer to −1 indicate a stronger inverse association. "B minus A" is the
change in correlation under the request implementation; the final column counts
how many leave-one-year-out checks retain a stronger absolute correlation than
baseline.

### Figures

Figures show the programme total (all methods, excluding condoms) and the
long-acting methods (implant + IUCD). A point for 2020 shows 2020 CYP and births
in 2021.

```{r}
#| label: fig-counts
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-cap: "Counts: CYP (thousands) and recorded facility births in the following year (thousands)."
fig_dat <- function(basis) {
  d <- cyp_decay_series[group %in% c("All methods", "Implant + IUCD (long-acting)") &
                           measure %in% names(mcol)]
  cy <- d[, .(group, measure, year,
              value = if (basis == "Counts") cyp_value / 1e3 else cyp_per_1000_wra,
              panel = if (basis == "Counts") "CYP (thousands)" else "CYP per 1,000 women 15–49")]
  b <- d[measure == "A. Standard" & !is.na(births_next),
         .(group, measure = "Births in following year", year,
           value = if (basis == "Counts") births_next / 1e3 else births_next_per_1000_wra,
           panel = if (basis == "Counts") "Births in N+1 (thousands)" else "Births in N+1 per 1,000 women 15–49")]
  rbind(cy, b)
}
trend_plot <- function(basis) {
  d <- fig_dat(basis)
  lev <- unique(d$panel)
  d[, panel := factor(panel, levels = lev)]
  cols <- c(mcol, "Births in following year" = "black")
  ggplot(d, aes(year, value, colour = measure, linetype = measure)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    facet_grid(panel ~ group, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols,
                        labels = c("A. Standard" = "A. Standard baseline",
                                   "D. Full proposal" = "B. Request implementation",
                                   "Births in following year" = "Births in N+1"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("A. Standard" = "solid", "D. Full proposal" = "solid",
                     "Births in following year" = "solid"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2025, 2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#e8edf2"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
trend_plot("Counts")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-cap: "All methods, excluding condoms: CYP in year N against recorded births in year N+1. Points are labelled by CYP year. The title of each panel gives the correlation."
scatter_plot <- function(basis, grp = "All methods") {
  d <- cyp_decay_series[group == grp & measure %in% names(mcol) & !is.na(births_next)]
  d[, `:=`(x = if (basis == "Counts") cyp_value / 1e3 else cyp_per_1000_wra,
           y = if (basis == "Counts") births_next / 1e3 else births_next_per_1000_wra)]
  r <- d[, .(r = cor(x, y)), by = measure]
  d[r, on = "measure", lab := sprintf("%s (r = %.2f)", measure, i.r)]
  ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = measure), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = year), size = 2.8, vjust = -0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~lab, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = mcol, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x = if (basis == "Counts") "CYP in year N (thousands)" else "CYP per 1,000 women 15–49, year N",
         y = if (basis == "Counts") "Births in year N+1 (thousands)" else "Births per 1,000 women 15–49, year N+1") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#e8edf2"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
scatter_plot("Counts")
```

### Results

For next-year facility births (N+1), yearly values, counts (rates per 1,000
women aged 15–49 in brackets):

- **Implants:** baseline `r rv("Implant", "A. Standard")`
  (`r rv("Implant", "A. Standard", "Rates")`); request implementation
  `r rv("Implant", "D. Full proposal")`
  (`r rv("Implant", "D. Full proposal", "Rates")`).
- **IUCDs:** baseline `r rv("IUCD", "A. Standard")`
  (`r rv("IUCD", "A. Standard", "Rates")`); request implementation
  `r rv("IUCD", "D. Full proposal")`
  (`r rv("IUCD", "D. Full proposal", "Rates")`).
- **All methods, excluding condoms:** baseline `r rv("All methods", "A. Standard")`
  (`r rv("All methods", "A. Standard", "Rates")`); request implementation
  `r rv("All methods", "D. Full proposal")`
  (`r rv("All methods", "D. Full proposal", "Rates")`).
- **Sensitivity to individual years:** in `r jk_request("All methods")` of ten leave-one-year-out checks, the request implementation's all-methods count series had a stronger absolute correlation than baseline. This does not address confounding or the pre-2015 assumption.

Previous-year births (N−1) are retained as a secondary alignment check in the
table. Neither alignment establishes a contraceptive effect: annual trends,
facility-only birth counts, reporting changes, and the warm-up assumption can
all influence these correlations.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Limitations
- Ten yearly points, and both series trend. Births rose to a peak around
  2019–2020 and then fell while CYP kept rising, so the correlations are driven
  by the years after 2020. Spreading moves CYP later in time, and with a single
  turning point in births this test cannot separate a protection effect from a
  time shift that happens to fit.
- Confidence intervals are indicative only, because annual series are not
  independent.
- Recorded births are facility births, not national births.
- The leave-one-year-out check tests sensitivity to a single year, not
  confounding.
:::

**Conclusion.** The requested CYP series is compared with the standard
baseline, excluding condoms. The comparison includes revised factors,
decay-weighted allocation, and an assumed pre-2015 warm-up; it does not isolate
the effect of decay. Local continuation data are needed to validate the weights.

## Step 8. Limits and decisions needed

| Issue | Why it matters | Proposed action |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-2015 cohorts | DHIS starts in 2015; the request carries the 2015 count backward to initialize active cohorts | Treat early adjusted totals as assumption-dependent; compare with observed-only output as a supplementary sensitivity check |
| Weights | Only partly supplied; tail of IUCD profile is assumed | Replace with local continuation data (for example DHS calendar data) |
| Sterilisation | Permanent, but credited in one year | Decide: spread, or report separately |
| Pill factor | Request specifies 12 cycles per CYP; baseline uses 15 | Confirm whether the DHIS pill indicator represents combined-pill cycles or progestin-only packs before applying 12 |
| Implant factor | Programme uses 3.5, the proposal uses 2.5 | Confirm the factor to use as the reference |
| Condoms | Dominant in total CYP and counted at 100% use | Excluded from the headline comparison (switch `CYP_COMPARISON_INCLUDE_CONDOMS` in `wrangling.R`); report use scenarios separately |
| Data entry errors | One facility-month was 10,000 times its normal value; it is now corrected in `wrangling.R` and logged | Keep the residual-extreme check, and review any flagged facility-months |
| Births | Facility births only; ten points | Treat as descriptive; repeat with national births when available |

: Limits, why they matter, and proposed actions.

## Where the numbers come from

All counts come from `projects/dhis_hospital_mortality/wrangling.R` (national
sums of facility-level DHIS counts, 2015–2025). Every table on this page reads
objects saved by that script, including the programme comparison, the condom
share, the correlations and the data-correction log. The implant calculation in
Step 5 is repeated by hand on this page, and the page stops with an error if it
differs from the pipeline.
